oidc_jwt.description: Brokered OIDC login creates or links a local Keycloak user record rather than exposing the upstream subject as a standalone principal.
oidc_jwt.source: IdentityProviderRepresentation and Users endpoints in Keycloak Admin REST API
oidc_jwt.note: I4 checks must compare the upstream identity to the resulting local user/linkage, not expect a raw upstream subject-only principal.

oidc_jwt.description: User search is prefix-based by default and supports infix/exact syntax in the search parameter.
oidc_jwt.note: Multiple search hits are not identity collisions; use exact lookup when asserting principal uniqueness.

oidc_jwt.description: Brokered identities may link to an existing Keycloak user based on broker configuration such as trusted email and first-login/linking flows, causing different upstream identities to resolve to one downstream account.
oidc_jwt.source: IdentityProviderRepresentation.trustEmail, firstBrokerLoginFlowAlias, postBrokerLoginFlowAlias in Admin REST schema
oidc_jwt.note: This can look like a cross-user collision but is configuration-driven broker linking behavior.

oidc_jwt.description: User search endpoints use prefix/contains/exact semantics depending on parameters and quoting; broad search results are not proof of identity collision.
oidc_jwt.source: Users endpoint query parameter descriptions for search and exact
oidc_jwt.note: Use direct user-id lookup or exact filters before flagging I4 issues.

oidc_jwt.description: Changing identity provider or mapper configuration affects subsequent logins, while already-established local sessions may continue until logout/expiry.
oidc_jwt.source: Identity provider update endpoints and user/session logout endpoints in Keycloak Admin REST API
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag an existing session remaining valid after admin config change as a coherence bug unless the same in-flight request is inconsistently evaluated.

oidc_jwt.description: After admin updates to identity provider or mapper configuration, subsequent new logins are evaluated under the updated configuration.
oidc_jwt.note: A changed outcome after reconfiguration is expected; only stale acceptance under old config is suspicious.

oidc_jwt.description: Group listing may omit subGroups unless specific search parameters are used.
oidc_jwt.note: Missing subgroup data in a listing response is not evidence that group mappings were lost.

oidc_jwt.description: User logout revokes all sessions associated with the user rather than a single specified access token.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not interpret broad revocation as token confusion or overreach.

oidc_jwt.description: Replay protection for refresh tokens is optional and controlled by realm settings; access tokens remain bearer tokens and are not one-time by default.
oidc_jwt.note: Reusing bearer access tokens or refresh tokens when replay protection is disabled is by design.

oidc_jwt.description: Effective permissions can include roles granted through groups, composites, default scopes, and protocol/identity-provider mappers rather than only directly requested scopes.
oidc_jwt.source: ClientRepresentation.fullScopeAllowed, role mappings, groups, and protocol mapper schemas in Admin REST API
oidc_jwt.note: Extra claims or roles may be configuration-driven and not an authorization-binding bug.

oidc_jwt.constraint: Keycloak brokered OIDC/JWT login is not exposed as a direct admin REST 'login with JWT' endpoint in the provided documentation. The fuzzer MUST test oidc_jwt through the browser-style broker flow using start_oidc_auth -> exchange_code_for_token, and MUST NOT assume a direct POST token-verification endpoint exists.

For I1 issuer/trust-anchor tests, configure_jwt_validation MUST set the identity provider's config on the OIDC broker instance itself. If the IdP is not created or updated with the intended issuer/JWKS settings, any acceptance/rejection result is not attributable to JWT validation.

For I3 config-change sequences, after updating /admin/realms/{realm}/identity-provider/instances/{alias} or its mappers, the fuzzer MUST perform a NEW broker login. Existing local Keycloak sessions are separate from upstream validation and may remain valid by design.

For I3 mapper-tightening tests, modify_role_config MUST tighten the identity-provider mapper or role assignment logic, not merely edit unrelated display settings. Otherwise a successful re-login does not test stale authorization state.

Keycloak user search parameters have mixed matching semantics. /admin/realms/{realm}/users supports exact=true for username/email/firstName/lastName, while search supports prefix by default, *foo* infix, and "foo" exact. For I4 multi-identity tests, the fuzzer MUST NOT treat username/email query parameters as wildcard-capable unless using search semantics explicitly.

Identity provider instance listing/search uses search semantics documented as prefix (name*), contains (*name*), or exact ("name"). This applies to administrative lookup only, not authentication constraints. The fuzzer MUST NOT infer that IdP claim matching supports wildcards from these admin search endpoints.

Group lookup/search endpoints also distinguish exact boolean from search/q behavior. For I4 collision tests involving groups, the fuzzer MUST use direct ID lookups or exact searches when verifying mappings; fuzzy search can return multiple groups and create false collision signals.

RealmRepresentation contains numeric session/token controls including accessTokenLifespan, ssoSessionIdleTimeout, ssoSessionMaxLifespan, clientSessionIdleTimeout, clientSessionMaxLifespan, offlineSessionIdleTimeout, offlineSessionMaxLifespan, actionTokenGeneratedByAdminLifespan, and refreshTokenMaxReuse. The provided documentation does not define sentinel meanings for 0 or -1 for these fields. The fuzzer MUST NOT assume 0 means disabled or default, and SHOULD probe actual behavior before using boundary values.

refreshTokenMaxReuse is a token reuse budget parameter. Any verification call that refreshes or otherwise consumes refresh-token reuse before the target action can exhaust the budget. If the fuzzer performs both a verification step and a subsequent refresh-dependent action, the minimum safe value is at least 2.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, the sequence MUST include a control login through the same broker using a valid upstream token and the same IdP configuration. Without a control, a failed broker login may be caused by broken IdP setup rather than exp/nbf enforcement.

Keycloak admin verification endpoints are admin-authenticated, not session-self-service in the provided documentation. The fuzzer MUST interpret verify_granted_identity and verify_entity_details as out-of-band inspection of the created local user/session state, not proof that the session token itself can call a self-lookup endpoint.

For I5 authorization tests, resource access in the provided admin API is best modeled via authorization evaluation endpoints, not by reading an application resource with the user bearer token. The fuzzer MUST avoid treating admin-side policy evaluation as equivalent to end-user resource fetch unless the test oracle accounts for this distinction.

Identity provider mappers accept config as a string map, but the provided documentation does not specify claim value type coercion rules. For I5 numeric coercion tests, the fuzzer SHOULD explicitly test whether numeric upstream claims are stringified, truncated, or rejected when mapped into roles/groups/attributes, because cross-type behavior is undocumented.

Keycloak realm creation is a prerequisite for all admin setup under /admin/realms/{realm}/... . The fuzzer MUST run create_tenant before any OIDC/JWT broker, client, role, group, or resource configuration.

For I1 issuer/trust-anchor tests, configure_jwt_validation MUST set the identity provider config fields that define the upstream issuer and key source (for example issuer/JWKS-related entries inside IdentityProviderRepresentation.config). If these are omitted or left permissive, issuer and signing-key validation may not be meaningfully exercised.

For I3 config-change tests against brokered OIDC, the fuzzer MUST update the existing identity provider instance via PUT /admin/realms/{realm}/identity-provider/instances/{alias} and then perform a NEW login. A changed result after admin reconfiguration is by design; only stale acceptance of old trust/config after the update is a failure.

Identity-provider mapper matching semantics are mapper-specific and are not described in the OpenAPI schema beyond opaque config maps. The fuzzer MUST NOT assume wildcard or regex support in mapper config values. For I4 multi-identity scenarios, do not set literal '*' expecting wildcard behavior unless the specific mapper type documentation confirms it.

Users search semantics are not exact by default. GET /admin/realms/{realm}/users uses prefix/infix/exact search behavior depending on query parameters and quoting, while exact=true only affects certain fields. For I4 collision checks, verify_entity_details_by_name MUST use exact=true with direct username/email filters where possible, not broad search strings.

Identity provider listing/search also supports prefix/contains/exact semantics in the search query. This is administrative discovery only; the fuzzer MUST NOT use provider search results as identity-binding evidence for I4.

Keycloak token freshness tests MUST include a control login using a valid token/time window alongside the attack token. Without a control, rejection at the broker or token endpoint cannot be distinguished from broken IdP/client setup.

Numeric sentinel analysis: RealmRepresentation contains many TTL-style integer fields (accessTokenLifespan, ssoSessionIdleTimeout, ssoSessionMaxLifespan, clientSessionIdleTimeout, clientSessionMaxLifespan, actionTokenGeneratedByAdminLifespan, actionTokenGeneratedByUserLifespan, oauth2DeviceCodeLifespan, refreshTokenMaxReuse, notBefore), but the OpenAPI excerpt does not define sentinel meanings for 0 or -1. The fuzzer MUST NOT assume 0 means disabled or literal zero, nor that -1 disables enforcement; verify actual runtime behavior before drawing I2 conclusions.

Session-use budget analysis: no per-token use-count parameter is documented for OIDC access tokens in this Keycloak excerpt. Verification calls still consume token lifetime/time budget, but there is no documented num_uses-style counter to configure. Do not misclassify expiry-based failures as use-budget exhaustion.

For I5 scope/authorization tests, Keycloak authorization decisions depend on client scopes, roles, protocol mappers, and authorization resources/policies. The fuzzer MUST seed both the protected resource and the downstream role/group mappings; a successful broker login alone does not imply resource access should succeed.

For I5 token-exchange tests, token_exchange MUST specify audience explicitly when testing audience binding. Reusing the token endpoint without audience can produce tokens scoped for the requesting client by design, which would mask audience-validation issues.

For I4 principal-binding tests, trustEmail=true and mapper configurations that link by email can intentionally merge identities sharing the same email. If testing sub-based separation, the fuzzer MUST avoid email-linking configurations or treat same-email merges as configuration-driven rather than automatic broker collapse.

For I4/I5 group mapping tests, create_group_alias is implemented through identity-provider mappers, not a dedicated alias endpoint. The exact mapper type and config determine whether upstream groups are added, synced, or ignored. The fuzzer MUST read back mapper config after creation and avoid assuming one mapper type behaves like another.

For I2 revocation tests, revoking a user via POST /admin/realms/{realm}/users/{user-id}/logout removes all sessions for that user, not a single explicit bearer token. The fuzzer MUST attribute subsequent failures to user-session revocation semantics, not token-specific blacklist behavior.
Keycloak OIDC broker testing requires a realm tenant. The fuzzer MUST create a realm before configuring identity providers, roles, groups, clients, or sessions.

For I1 issuer/trust-anchor tests, configure_jwt_validation MUST set the identity provider config on the broker instance itself. If the IdP alias remains pointed at the original issuer/JWKS, later login results do not test trust rotation or issuer enforcement.

For I3 jwt_signing_key_rotation tests, after updating the brokered OIDC identity provider trust settings, the fuzzer SHOULD call /admin/realms/{realm}/identity-provider/instances/{alias}/reload-keys before the attack login. Otherwise stale cached keys may cause false positives or false negatives.

For I3 config-change sequences, Keycloak admin updates are by design applied to NEW logins. A valid coherence test must compare pre-change and post-change logins under the same realm and IdP alias, not expect an already-issued session to retroactively change identity.

RealmRepresentation.refreshTokenMaxReuse is a numeric replay-control parameter. Value 0 does not mean single-use; it means no extra reuse restriction when revokeRefreshToken is enabled. Never assume 0 disables refresh tokens or makes them one-time.

RealmRepresentation.revokeRefreshToken and refreshTokenMaxReuse jointly control refresh-token replay. Verification calls that use the access token do not consume refresh-token reuse budget, but any refresh/token reissue calls do. If a test sequence needs more than one refresh, refreshTokenMaxReuse MUST be set accordingly.

RealmRepresentation access/session lifespan fields are literal seconds, not sentinel-controlled durations in the provided schema: accessTokenLifespan, ssoSessionIdleTimeout, ssoSessionMaxLifespan, clientSessionIdleTimeout, clientSessionMaxLifespan, accessCodeLifespan, accessCodeLifespanLogin, accessCodeLifespanUserAction, actionTokenGeneratedByAdminLifespan, actionTokenGeneratedByUserLifespan. The fuzzer MUST treat 0 as literal zero/invalid unless separately documented by deployment behavior; do not assume 0 means default.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, the sequence MUST include a control login using a valid token/time window in the same realm and client configuration. Without a control, token rejection may be caused by broken client/IdP setup rather than freshness enforcement.

Keycloak user search parameters have explicit matching semantics. /admin/realms/{realm}/users supports exact boolean and search syntax where default search is prefix-based, *foo* is infix, and "foo" is exact. For I4 multi-identity tests, do not treat username/email filters as wildcard authorization constraints; they are admin search helpers only.

Identity provider alias matching is exact path matching only because the alias is a path segment in /admin/realms/{realm}/identity-provider/instances/{alias} and broker endpoints. For multi-provider tests, the fuzzer MUST create separate aliases; wildcard alias values are not supported.

Identity-provider mapper config is an untyped string map in the admin schema. For I5 numeric coercion tests on claim/group mappers, the fuzzer SHOULD explicitly test whether numeric upstream claim values are coerced to strings by the mapper/provider configuration rather than assuming typed comparison.

For I4 cross-user-collision tests, trustEmail=true can cause downstream account linking/merging behavior based on email semantics rather than subject isolation. To test principal binding on upstream subject values, the fuzzer SHOULD disable trustEmail unless the test specifically targets email-based merge behavior.

For I4 tests, linkOnly=true on the identity provider changes behavior from login/auto-provisioning to account-linking semantics. The fuzzer MUST keep linkOnly=false for normal broker-login identity binding tests, otherwise login failures or merges may be by design.

For I5 group/role escalation tests, identity-provider mappers and group role mappings can legitimately add downstream roles beyond raw upstream token claims. The fuzzer MUST model effective permissions as upstream intent intersected with configured mappers, group memberships, and realm/client role mappings, not just direct token claims.

For token_exchange_wrong_audience and token_exchange_ignore_audience tests, the fuzzer MUST use the OIDC token endpoint with grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange and explicitly set audience. Testing without audience only exercises default token issuance behavior, not audience binding.

For token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, the fuzzer MUST compare exchanged-token scopes/claims against the original subject_token authorization and the requesting client's configured scopes. Keycloak may add claims through default/optional client scopes and protocol mappers; this is configuration-driven and must be accounted for before flagging I5.

For oidc_request_object_alg_none tests, start_oidc_auth may accept a request parameter only if the upstream/client configuration supports request objects. The fuzzer MUST ensure the target client and broker flow actually use request objects before interpreting acceptance or rejection as a signature-validation result.

verify_granted_identity uses /userinfo and returns OIDC claims, not full session metadata. The fuzzer MUST not interpret missing ttl/num_uses style fields as security failures; Keycloak's userinfo response is claim-centric rather than Vault-style token introspection.
